title: GUARD (fixed in d555917f07) — was: `argv+=( ... )` throws the positional parameters away and keeps the appended array ACROSS calls — zsh n=4 <1,2,3,X> three times, zshrs n=1 <X>, n=2 <X,X>, n=3 <X,X,X>

retired.fix_commit_subject: params: argv+= appends to pparams; keyed read of a hashed local shadow
retired.why: params: argv+= appends to pparams; keyed read of a hashed local shadow — item 1. `argv`/`@`/`*` are IPDEF9 rows bound to `&pparams` (Src/params.c:392-393, :430) whose array GSU has no storage of its own, so assignaparam's ASSPM_AUGMENT arm (:3514) must take the append offset from that getter; zshrs was reading the paramtab node's `u_arr`, a process-global slot that is empty for these names and never swapped per call — which produced both the discard and the cross-call leak this fixture recorded.
retired.evidence: re-verified first-hand by scripts/compsys_regressions.py under --variants: the fixture cell scored NOW-PASSES -> NOW-PASSES -> NOW-PASSES, and every variant and control of it came back CONTROL-HOLDS/NOW-PASSES. The runner reported the binary MOVED since the stamp (6420c23cecc13c35 -> 723088f811cdd366), which is the 'somebody fixed the bug' branch of the two the README names, not the 'the fixture was wrong' one.
retired.kept_because: a fixed bug is worth more as a guard than as a deleted file: the cell stays in the evidence base and the gate now FAILS if the divergence comes back.

guard_verified.against: /opt/homebrew/bin/zshrs -> Cellar/zshrs-all/0.12.49/bin/zshrs, the Homebrew-installed RELEASE build of the same version, 18273880 bytes, sha256 fb94500d8e1c32e7, built 2026-08-30 06:20:45 — before d555917f07 (08:04) and 44a3b4841c (08:32), so it still carries the bug
guard_verified.note: the flip is only worth something if the gate would CATCH the bug coming back, so it was pointed at a build that still has it: `compsys_regressions.py --zshrs /opt/homebrew/bin/zshrs --only argv_append_discards_positionals`. It reported CONTROL-MOVED and exited 1. The harness detail it produced there is the same one observed_when_diverging records, so the guard fails on THIS bug and not merely on some difference.

observed.measured: 2026-08-30, commit 44a3b4841c, a byte-identical copy of target/debug/zshrs, passed with --zshrs (zshrs 0.12.49, 101620888 bytes, sha256 723088f811cdd366) vs zsh 5.9.2 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.4.0)
observed.notes: byte-identical stdout and exit status across all three `f 1 2 3` calls: both shells now print `n=4 argv=<1,2,3,X>` three times, where zshrs used to print n=1 <X>, n=2 <X,X>, n=3 <X,X,X>. STDERR is not compared (compare_stderr false, as before).

observed_when_diverging.notes: Two defects in one line of shell. (a) the append REPLACES the positional parameters instead of extending them, so `$@` is only what was appended; (b) whatever it appends to is not per-frame — the third call sees the two X's the first two left behind, which is why $# climbs 1,2,3 instead of staying 4. `argv=( $argv X )`, `set -- "$@" X` and the same append on a `local -a` array are all pinned as controls and all agree, so the variable is the `+=` form on `argv` specifically, not appends and not argv. Why this is in a COMPLETION evidence base: `Completion/Base/Core/_description` builds its zformat spec list with exactly this append (line 83), so every description compsys renders picks up the leftovers — the upstream Y0*.ztst run in tests/ztst_compsys/ shows it as `DESCRIPTION:{h:file}` where zsh emits `DESCRIPTION:{file}`, and that single misparse accounts for a large share of the failing assertions there.
observed_when_diverging.recorded_under: commit 3b4a01f0cd, target/debug/zshrs zshrs 0.12.49 (101601256 bytes, 2026-08-30 05:50:47), zsh 5.9.2 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.4.0) — this is the divergence AS MEASURED BEFORE d555917f07. It is history, not current behaviour; the fixture now asserts the two shells AGREE.

controls.note: the ASSIGN form of the same append. Agrees (PASS, byte-identical stdout and exit status), which is what makes `+=` the variable
`set --` reaching the same end state. Agrees, so the positional-parameter machinery itself is not broken
`+=` on an ordinary local array. Agrees, so array append is not broken either — only append onto `argv`

variants.note: WHEN THIS FIXTURE DIVERGED: the shortest witness, and the one the finding was reported as: zsh prints a/b/X, zshrs prints X alone. Observed: 3 line(s) differ — row0 zsh 'a' vs zshrs 'X', row1 zsh 'b' vs '<absent>', row2 zsh 'X' vs '<absent>'  NOW: agrees (NOW-PASSES -> NOW-PASSES -> NOW-PASSES; harness detail 'byte-identical stdout and exit status').
